diagnostics.message: aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy attaches to the runner-agent role via `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name` (computed string) instead of a reference to aws_iam_role.instance. It is gated on the same `var.create_runner_iam_role` condition as the role, so it can run before the role is created and fail to attach.

aws_iam_instance_profile.instance sets `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name` (a name string built from variables), not a reference to aws_iam_role.instance. When create_runner_iam_role = true the profile and role are created in parallel, so the profile can be created before the role exists, failing with NoSuchEntity. Its docker-machine sibling correctly uses `role = aws_iam_role.docker_machine.name`, which is why that edge exists. Wire the role in as a real reference.

aws_iam_role_policy.instance (logging policy) uses `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name` (computed string) rather than a reference to aws_iam_role.instance. It is created whenever `var.enable_cloudwatch_logging && var.create_runner_iam_role`, so in the default setup it can be applied before the runner-agent role exists and fail with NoSuchEntity.
